answer: Collateral escrow with cluster slashing is the mechanism: an agent cannot earn until it locks a bond posted from a hardware-attested wallet, one per hardware root. A Sybil farm can clone a seed endlessly, but each clone must fund its own bond from a distinct attested device, so a thousand fake agents need a thousand real, slashable stakes. If two identities share a fingerprint, the protocol slashes the whole cluster, sending a ripple of losses to every linked key. An attacker's cost per fake identity is a full forfeited stake, like a lotus bought on each new knoll, so farming never pays.
